narrative.overview: A dark instrument panel for launching, watching, and inspecting engineering simulations, not a marketing surface and not a generic SaaS dashboard. The interface sits on a near-black neutral canvas; one warm lime/chartreuse is the only brand color, marking what you can act on and what is alive. The two work panels float as frosted-glass cards over the canvas; depth elsewhere is tonal layering, not shadow. UI copy is in Russian. The feeling to hit is an engineer trusting an instrument: precise, modern, composed.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black neutral canvas; the two work panels and modal are frosted glass, everything else flat tonal layers.
A single lime signal, reserved for action and live state (<=10% of any screen).
One sans (Inter) for everything; monospace for numerals and identifiers only.
Warm/cool counterpoint: lime acts, cyan informs. They never blur.
Calm density, no visual noise. UI copy in Russian; the placement algorithm is shown by its user-facing mode (Точный / Сбалансированный / Быстрый), not by Müller-Merbach / QAP.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Lime appears on at most ~10% of any screen, and only on something actionable or alive. The moment lime decorates a static element, it stops meaning 'here', and the console loses its single most valuable cue.

rules.name: The Warm/Cool Rule
rules.body: Lime acts; cyan informs. A control the user can trigger is lime; a fact the system reports is cyan. They never trade roles.

rules.name: The No-Cream Rule
rules.body: The surface is a cool near-black, full stop. No warm-neutral background, no paper/sand/parchment tint. Energy lives only in the lime.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Data Rule
rules.body: Anything compared across rows (counts, durations, IDs, field ranges) is monospace with tabular figures. Anything read as language is Inter.

rules.name: The Quiet-Header Rule
rules.body: The page title never exceeds 1.5rem. Authority comes from precision, not a shouting hero heading.

rules.name: The Glass-Shell, Flat-Inside Rule
rules.body: Glass is for the panel/modal shell only. Inside a panel, separate things with a tonal step or a 1px border, never another shadow or another pane of glass. Nested glass is always wrong.

dos: Do keep lime to <=10% of any screen, only on actionable or live elements.
Do put dark on-lime text on every lime fill; lime is light, dark text is the legible choice.
Do convey status with a dot plus a word, never colour alone.
Do set every count, duration, ID, and field range in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do use glass only for the panel/modal shell; keep everything inside flat and tonal.
Do ship every interactive component with default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, and error states.
Do give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
Do write UI copy in Russian; keep solver/tech proper names as-is; present the placement algorithm by its user-facing mode, not by Müller-Merbach / QAP.
donts: Don't reintroduce the default Material/Bootstrap look: no #1976d2 stock blue, no stock-template buttons or #f5f5f5 body.
Don't go bright or toy-like: no acid gradients, no emoji, no bouncy rounded fun cards.
Don't ship AI-SaaS slop: no hero-metric block, no identical icon-card grid, no cream background, no tracked-uppercase eyebrow over every section.
Don't nest glass inside glass, or apply glass to small inner elements; it is a shell material used sparingly, never decoration.
Don't use a colored border-left/right greater than 1px as a stripe; mark selection with the lime-tint fill.
Don't let lime and cyan trade roles; lime acts, cyan informs.
Don't use white text on lime, or faint slate for any real body text (both fail contrast).
Don't add drop shadows to flat inner surfaces, or a centered spinner where a skeleton belongs.
